text.text: For comprehensive information on the HHI,
The Herth Hope Index (HHI) yields a total score ranging from 12 to 84, with higher scores
indicating greater levels of hope, as well as three subscale scores ranging from 4 to 28:
- Sense of temporality and future (Items 1, 2, 6 [reverse-scored], and 11): Assesses cognitive-
temporal aspects of hope, including belief that each day has potential, maintaining a positive
outlook, having short and long-term goals, and experiencing confidence about the future. Higher
scores indicate stronger future orientation and goal-directed thinking.
- Positive readiness and expectancy (Items 4, 7, 10, and 12): Measures affective-behavioural
aspects of hope, including the ability to see possibilities in difficult situations, sense of direction,
recognition of life's value and worth, and capacity to recall happy memories. Higher scores
suggest greater emotional resilience and readiness to act on hope.
- Interconnectedness with self and others (Items 3 [reverse-scored], 5, 8, and 9): Evaluates
affiliative-contextual aspects of hope, including feelings of connection versus isolation, presence
of comforting or spiritual beliefs, inner strength, and ability to give and receive care and love.
Higher scores indicate stronger interpersonal connections and beliefs that sustain hope.
